metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast bias by 5–15% relative to recent highs.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1–2 days above recent peak, then apply gradual decay.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast upward by 3–8% for the first 3–5 days of sentiment shift.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is mixed or neutral; add 2–5% buffer to forecast if sentiment variance > 0.5 over last 5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture late-cycle momentum; increase forecast by 1–3% for days 25–30 if sentiment is positive and price has been trending upward.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough if sentiment is trending.
